name: hearing loss overview
title: Hearing loss: the Weber and Rinne together split conductive (ear canal; otitis media; a fixed or broken middle ear) from sensorineural (sudden, an emergency; gradual and symmetric; one-sided and progressive, a vestibular schwannoma until proven otherwise); each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment

root.title: Hearing loss: is sound BLOCKED before the cochlea, or is the cochlea or nerve DAMAGED?
lines: 512 Hz tuning forks, ALWAYS both: Weber on the midline (where is it loudest?) + Rinne (mastoid, then beside the ear)
a SUDDEN conductive loss can wait; a SUDDEN sensorineural loss is an EMERGENCY

groups.title: CONDUCTIVE
lines: Weber → the AFFECTED ear · Rinne there: bone > air
audiogram: bone normal, air down (an air-bone gap)

groups.title: SENSORINEURAL
lines: Weber → the NORMAL ear · Rinne: air > bone
audiogram: bone down, air the same as bone
damage to cochlea or nerve cannot be repaired

head: h
Ear canal
wax · foreign body · exostoses · otitis externa
pres: • bacterial: itchy, painful, swollen, sore on pulling the pinna
• fungal: severe itch, less pain, after antibiotics

head: h
Otitis media
the commonest middle ear cause
inv: Fluid in BOTH ears for 3 months
tx: or watch 48-72 h in lower-risk children · treat pain
• effusion both ears > 3 months + > 20 dB loss in the better ear

head: h
Drum or ossicles
perforation · otosclerosis · longitudinal fracture
pres: • otosclerosis: NORMAL drum, no trauma or infection
• fracture (80%, side blow): unconscious, bleeding from or behind the drum
inv: otosclerosis: conductive or mixed, Carhart's notch
tx: • perforation: keep dry, 80% heal; else tympanoplasty

head: h
SUDDEN sensorineural
onset < 3 days · EMERGENCY
tx: Steroids by mouth or into the ear

head: h
Gradual, symmetric
presbycusis · noise · ototoxic drugs
pres: • presbycusis: commonest, HIGH pitches first, 30% over 65, 50% over 75
• aminoglycosides, cisplatin, carboplatin, vincristine, loop diuretics

head: h
ONE-sided, progressive
vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma)
pres: ~commonest cerebellopontine angle mass · both sides = NF2
